sections.content:
Population change in Ealing in 2032

The population in Ealing is projected to increase from 370,129 people in 2022 to 384,268 people in 2032.

Despite an overall increase in the population, there is projected to be a fall in net internal migration, which will decrease the population by 63,573 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Ealing
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Ealing, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 18,784, with 42,608 births and 23,824 deaths in Ealing between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Ealing by 5.1%, compared with an increase of 6.0% in London and an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 63,573, with 295,558 people moving to the area and 359,131 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Ealing by 17.2%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 874, with 6,964 people moving to the area and 7,838 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Ealing by 0.2%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 59,479, with 115,168 people moving to the area and 55,688 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Ealing by 16.1%, compared with an increase of 14.7% in London and an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Age profile in Ealing in 2032

The median age in Ealing is projected to rise from 37 years in 2022 to 38 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 14% of the population in Ealing are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 12% in 2022.

sections.title: The 10 to 19 age group are set to see the largest change in Ealing between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Ealing is projected to stay the same, at around 70%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 168 to 187 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Ealing?

In 2032, 19% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 23% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Ealing between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 9% to 7%
